agents.note:
*** SPRINT 73 / V0.29.28 COMPLETE -- 4 of 4 (US-549 I-043, US-550 I-044, US-543 A-4 parity guard, US-545 A-18 BT bond self-heal). Nothing left to pick up; the sprint now owes only its Pi-side legs, listed at the bottom. ***

*** THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE ONE THE LAST NOTE PREDICTED: I RESUMED A CUT-OFF US-545 ITERATION WHERE THE IMPLEMENTATION WAS FINISHED, POLISHED, 2377 LINES, UNCOMMITTED -- AND THE GATE HAD NEVER BEEN RUN. Running it found two real defects, one of which made the entire story a no-op on the Pi. NEVER INFER GREEN FROM POLISH. If you inherit a working tree that looks done, the gate is the first thing you run, not the last. ***

DEFECT 1, and it is the previous note's own warning coming true verbatim ('a mock-driven test proves the mock works and says nothing about the path that runs on the Pi'): the new systemd unit declared NO PYTHONPATH, so its ExecStart `-m src.pi.obdii.bond_self_heal` died at `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pi'` (src/pi/obdii/__init__.py opens `from pi.display import ...`, which needs <repo>/src on sys.path). 51 green tests drove the healer through a fake; ZERO ran the ExecStart. The deploy guard asserted `'bond_self_heal' in execStart`, which passes over `-m pi.obdii.X` and `-m src.pi.obdii.X` EQUALLY -- and this repo genuinely ships both conventions (`-m pi.splash.states_http_server` beside `-m src.pi.power.power_watch`), so it was a coin flip the guard could not see. The unit would have installed, enabled, and been silently inert every boot.

*** ADOPT THIS FOR EVERY NEW SYSTEMD UNIT -- it is ~20 lines and it is the only thing separating a unit that RUNS from one that merely PARSES: subprocess-run the unit's own ExecStart module, with the unit's own PYTHONPATH (both parsed OUT of the unit, not restated), and assert it reaches a known usage exit code. Add a NEGATIVE CONTROL with PYTHONPATH unset that must fail -- otherwise you cannot tell whether the directive is load-bearing or decoration. See tests/deploy/test_bond_selfheal_deploy.py::TestExecStartActuallyImports. Mutation evidence came free: both guards were RED against the real defect, green after the fix. ***

DEFECT 2: tests/deploy/test_no_radio_disable_in_project.py (the BL-025 guard) went RED on `bluetoothctl power off` in the wedge reset -- a correct catch, since a radio left dark IS the 07-03 outage. AC1 explicitly requires that reset, so it takes the guard's own escape hatch `radio-guard-exempt`. TWO things made that defensible rather than a loosening: it is a runtime D-Bus property NOT an rfkill soft-block (systemd-rfkill PERSISTS soft-blocks across reboots -- that is how 07-03 got sticky, so this cannot survive a reboot even if wrong), AND the justification is TESTED not asserted (two tests drive the early-return paths between the power-off and the `finally` and assert the adapter ends POWERED). GOTCHA: the marker must be ON the offending line -- _strippedLines() drops whole-line `#` comments before matching, so a marker on the line above silently vanishes.

THIRD TRAP, smaller but general: systemd spells it `Environment=PYTHONPATH=...`, so a parsed-unit dict keys it under `Environment`. My first cut read directives['PYTHONPATH'] -> []. In a PRESENCE check that failed loudly and I caught it; in an ABSENCE check it would have passed over any unit at all. Same shape as US-550's Grep blindspot: an empty result is evidence ONLY once you know the lookup can see the thing.

US-545 AS BUILT: src/pi/obdii/bond_self_heal.py + deploy/eclipse-bond-selfheal.service + a deploy-pi.sh install step + a start-only polkit grant. It is a STANDALONE UNIT, not a method, because the heal must `systemctl stop eclipse-obd` first (AC2) -- an in-process heal would be a process asking systemd to kill it mid-call; the logger only REQUESTS it via `systemctl start --no-block`. Bounded (AC3) to one re-pair per boot, budget consumed BEFORE the work. 8 outcomes, one per remedy, so AC4's loud-surface is a distinct outcome + operatorAction rather than a generic failure. SUBTLE + WORTH KEEPING: a de-bonded device and an unreadable bluez give the IDENTICAL all-False BondState, so the verdict is taken against an ADAPTER reading too -- no reading means UNKNOWN and NO action in either direction, or a slow-booting bluetooth.service gets 'healed' in response to our own blindness.

GATE: tests/pi/obdii/ (all) + tests/deploy/test_bond_selfheal_deploy.py -- EXIT 0 on the final consolidated run; also green: test_unit_manifest (10th canonical unit), test_no_radio_disable_in_project, test_deploy_pi, test_deploy_invariants, test_rfkill_unblock_install, test_obdctl_install, test_bt_link_drop_transport_reset. ruff clean on 8 touched .py files. UNLIKE my last three stories this one DOES touch src/ (obd_connection.py's connect path), so flag tests/pi/obdii/ to PM for the integration re-run. I did NOT stage .deploy-version -- it is a deploy artifact modified in the tree, not mine.

ENVIRONMENT (all still true, all still biting): `make` is NOT on PATH -- exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check <file>`. pytest config SUPPRESSES the `N passed` line -- trust the exit code. Glob over the repo root TIMES OUT (SMB); use `git ls-files | grep`. THE GREP TOOL CANNOT SEE specs/UI/dist/ (gitignored-but-tracked) -- use `git grep`. Bash rejects `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` and compound `&&` chains re-prompt -- one command per call. A targeted pytest batch WILL sometimes exceed the 120s timeout and background; this session that was survivable because the completion notification arrives IN-iteration, but do not rely on it -- prefer small synchronous batches.

STILL OWED, Pi-side (batch these on the next deploy+boot; NONE are closable on the dev box): US-545 -- clear the bond (`bluetoothctl remove 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB`), reboot, confirm detect+re-pair-or-surface via `journalctl -u eclipse-bond-selfheal -u eclipse-obd | grep 'BOND SELF-HEAL'` and `systemctl show eclipse-bond-selfheal -p Before` (must list eclipse-obd); ENGINE ON, since the OBDLink LX is bus-powered off the OBD port and is genuinely absent engine-off. US-550 -- `systemctl show splash-boot.service -p Environment -p User` must read /run/user/1000 NOT /run/user/0. US-549 -- `journalctl -u splash-grace.service | grep '[shutdown-splash] terminal'` on the next clean shutdown. ASSERT AGAINST THE JOURNAL / `systemctl show`, NEVER unit text -- trusting unit text is exactly how the US-545 DOA survived. US-543 -- PM call on what 'standing CI' means beyond a pytest file, plus the testcontainers+Docker enablement US-464 owes. Prior sprint's F-126 debts + the I-us536 autoRotateS:0 resolver defect unchanged.
